Container.Name: enphase2mqtt
Container.Overview:
Bridges an Enphase IQ Gateway (Envoy) to your MQTT broker, using Home Assistant style discovery.
Your solar installation then shows up on its own in Jeedom, Home Assistant, or any other MQTT Discovery consumer.
EVERY PANEL, NOT JUST THE TOTAL: Each microinverter becomes its own device, with power, energy today, lifetime energy, DC voltage, DC current and temperature. DC voltage and current are what let you spot a panel that is failing or shaded, long before the total production says anything. Most Envoy bridges only publish the aggregate meters.
READ LOCALLY, NOT FROM THE CLOUD: Everything is read straight from the gateway on your LAN. The Enphase cloud is contacted once, to obtain the local access token, which is then stored and renewed automatically. Built on pyenphase, the library behind the official Home Assistant Enphase integration, so firmware differences are probed rather than assumed.
CURATED, NOT DUMPED: Around 105 entities on a three phase installation with ten panels, and every one of them carries a value. Aggregates the gateway leaves permanently at zero are not published, and grid voltage and frequency are published once rather than once per meter.
ROBUST: Discovery and states are replayed on every reconnection to the broker, so a broker restart cannot leave the bridge silently out of sync. An MQTT Last Will reports the bridge going down. A gateway reboot or a network glitch flips the bridge to offline and it retries, rather than dying.
REQUIREMENTS: An MQTT broker, the IP address of your Envoy, and your Enlighten account (the one used by the Enphase app). On firmware 7 and above the account is needed to obtain and renew the local token.
Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Enphase Energy.
Container.Requires: An MQTT broker, the LAN address of an Enphase IQ Gateway (Envoy), and an Enlighten account. The gateway must already be commissioned.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: enphase envoy iq gateway solar photovoltaic pv microinverter panel mqtt jeedom homeassistant home assistant discovery

Config.Name: Envoy address
Config.Description: IP address or hostname of your Enphase IQ Gateway on the LAN.

Config.Name: Enlighten username
Config.Description: Your Enphase Enlighten account, the same one used by the mobile app. Needed to obtain and renew the local token on firmware 7 and above.

Config.Name: Enlighten password
Config.Description: Password of the Enlighten account. Only sent to Enphase when a new token is needed.

Config.Name: MQTT broker host
Config.Description: IP address or hostname of your MQTT broker.

Config.Name: MQTT broker port
Config.Description: Port of your MQTT broker.

Config.Name: MQTT username
Config.Description: Leave empty if your broker allows anonymous connections.

Config.Name: MQTT password
Config.Description: Leave empty if your broker allows anonymous connections.

Config.Name: Config folder
Config.Description: Strongly recommended: this is where the access token is stored. Without it, every restart asks Enphase for a new token.

Config.Name: Publish each panel
Config.Description: true creates one device per microinverter, with power, energy, DC voltage, DC current and temperature. This is the main reason this bridge exists; set false for the meters alone.

Config.Name: Publish each phase
Config.Description: true creates one device per phase. Only useful on a three phase installation.

Config.Name: Panel names
Config.Description: Optional mapping from microinverter serial number to a name, comma separated, for instance 482233004696:Panneau 1, 482233004841:Panneau 2. Without it panels are numbered in ascending serial order, which will not necessarily match the numbering of an integration you are replacing.

Config.Name: Panel groups
Config.Description: Optional. Groups panels into arrays - a roof face, a string - and publishes one extra device per group with power, energy and installed peak summed over its members. Format is the mirror of panel names, group first: Roof East:482233004867+482233004853, Roof West:482232101756+482233004841. A serial the gateway does not know is dropped from the sum and logged.

Config.Name: Poll interval
Config.Description: Seconds between two reads of the gateway, minimum 15. The CT meters are near real time, but microinverters only report every five minutes or so, so polling faster mostly adds load.

Config.Name: Discovery topic prefix
Config.Description: Where discovery messages are published. Must match what your consumer listens on: homeassistant for Home Assistant, or the configuration topic of the Jeedom MQTT Discovery plugin.

Config.Name: State topic prefix
Config.Description: Root of the state topics. Jeedom users: this prefix must also be listed in the data topics setting of the MQTT Discovery plugin - the plugin only creates equipment for roots listed there. You do not have to type it: once its daemon has run, the plugin offers the roots it has discovered with a + button.

Config.Name: Bootstrap token
Config.Description: Optional. Leave empty: the bridge obtains a token from your Enlighten credentials on first start and stores it in the config folder.

Config.Name: Token file
Config.Description: Where the access token is persisted, mode 0600. Keep it inside the mounted config folder.

Config.Name: MQTT client id
Config.Description: Only change this if another client already uses that id on your broker.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR. DEBUG logs every topic published.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Timezone used for the log timestamps.
